platform_features.title: Fault injection
platform_features.summary: Ordered gateway rules inject protocol-correct AWS errors and cancellable latency by service, operation, Region and account, with probability, startup configuration, reset restoration, diagnostics and LocalStack Chaos API aliases.

platform_features.title: AWS wire protocols
platform_features.summary: AWS JSON 1.0/1.1, AWS Query, EC2 Query, REST XML/JSON, and Smithy RPC v2 CBOR through generated bindings.

platform_features.title: Identity and resource scope
platform_features.summary: Configured access-key accounts, IAM/STS credential lookup, regional and account-wide scopes, and optional SigV4 verification; general IAM permission evaluation is outside the subset.

platform_features.title: Transactional storage and persistence
platform_features.summary: Atomic callback transactions, in-memory storage, and optional SQLite commit persistence with resource reload on restart; runtime and in-flight state have separate limits.

platform_features.title: Cloudscape console
platform_features.summary: AWS-style dark dashboard with configurable widgets, a favorites bar of starred services, visit history, categorized service catalog with AWS icons, shared top-bar account/Region menus, resource inventory/details, IAM, S3, SQS, SNS, Lambda, DynamoDB, EventBridge, CloudWatch Logs and CloudWatch metrics/alarms/dashboard, API Gateway HTTP/REST, Step Functions, and EC2/VPC management workflows, recent requests, delivery history, and metrics through a separately served web console.

platform_features.title: Diagnostics
platform_features.summary: Health/resource endpoints, bounded request and delivery logs, model-sensitive body redaction, and Prometheus request metrics.

platform_features.title: Init hooks and reset
platform_features.summary: LocalStack-style boot, start, ready and shutdown scripts (also read from /etc/localstack/init) with a status endpoint, and a POST reset endpoint that clears all stored state and can re-run the ready scripts.

platform_features.title: CLI and SDK clients
platform_features.summary: Local endpoint overrides for AWS clients, CLI wrappers, and generated Go SDK-compatible APIs.

platform_features.title: Infrastructure workflows
platform_features.summary: Selected Terraform AWS provider workflows and local CloudFormation/SAM deployment through the registered resource-type subset.

platform_features.title: Runtime adapters
platform_features.summary: Docker Lambda execution and opt-in ECS Docker tasks, EKS k3s clusters, and ElastiCache Docker nodes; default optional adapters manage records.

platform_features.title: Cross-service event delivery
platform_features.summary: Supported notification, rule, and event-source workflows connect local service implementations and record delivery outcomes.

dynamodb.title: DynamoDB
dynamodb.summary: Store typed items and run expressions, transactions, streams, backups, exports, and PartiQL locally.
features: HASH and optional RANGE keys, global and local secondary indexes, sparse indexes and pagination
Nested condition, projection, filter, update and key expressions
Atomic batch and transaction operations with cancellation reasons and idempotency tokens
TTL sweeps, on-demand backups, latest-state point-in-time restores and S3 exports
PartiQL statements and transaction execution

AWS-style console with scoped table creation/deletion, primary and secondary keys, index management, typed item creation/editing/deletion, explicit query/scan with filters and pagination, capacity settings, TTL, tags, streams and Lambda connections
gaps: Index queries scan the table and are immediately consistent; no independent index storage
No throughput enforcement or capacity accounting; batch writes do not simulate throttling
Point-in-time restores retain the latest state, not historical snapshots
Legacy expression parameters, replica management and Kinesis streaming are outside the subset
Verify mode shows table inventory; item reads and management require signed CLI/SDK requests
Backups, restores, exports, PartiQL, batch and transaction operations use the AWS API rather than console forms

dynamodbstreams.title: DynamoDB Streams
dynamodbstreams.summary: Read the stream records written atomically with DynamoDB item changes.
features: List and describe streams, obtain shard iterators, and read records
Stream view types follow the table configuration
Lambda event source mappings consume stream records in-process
gaps: No shard splits or production-scale stream behavior
Only the fields selected in the profile are supported

s3.title: S3
s3.summary: Store objects, versions, multipart uploads, and event notifications in the shared local store.
features: Partition-wide bucket name uniqueness and ownership checks
Object CRUD, listing, metadata, tagging, copy, upload checksum validation, one byte range and conditional requests
Multipart upload lifecycle and atomic completion
Stored object checksums (CRC32, CRC32C, CRC64NVME by default, SHA-1, SHA-256) returned with ChecksumMode, composite and full-object multipart checksums, kept through copies and versions
Versioning, null versions and delete markers
Presigned requests, bucket CORS and notifications to SQS, SNS, Lambda and EventBridge
Bucket lifecycle and encryption configuration are stored
AWS-style console for scoped bucket creation, empty/delete, folder and object browsing, uploads/downloads/copies, version deletion, object tags and bucket configuration
gaps: Lifecycle rules do not expire or transition objects
Encryption settings are metadata; objects are not encrypted as an AWS S3 data plane would encrypt them
No website endpoint, POST uploads or general ACL/policy evaluation
Objects remain in memory even when commits are persisted to SQLite
REST payloads and completed multipart objects are limited to 64 MiB; larger objects need a streaming/storage design
Console uploads are limited to 1 MiB per file; object browsing and management require parse mode, while verify mode exposes bucket inventory only

elasticache.title: ElastiCache
elasticache.summary: Manage Redis, Valkey, and Memcached resources with an optional Docker cache runtime.
features: Cache clusters, replication groups, serverless caches, subnet groups and parameter groups
Single-shard replication groups with replica scaling, primary/reader endpoints, manual and test failover, and AUTH token updates
Engine metadata, tags and lifecycle events
Docker nodes expose allocated host ports and become available after readiness probes
Records mode returns metadata without starting cache processes
gaps: Cache data is lost when containers are removed on shutdown or restart; persistent mode retains metadata only
Host ports can change when nodes restart
Production networking, topology and failover behavior are not reproduced
Multi-shard cluster mode, snapshots/backups and RBAC users/user groups are outside the subset
Reset removes the cache containers it started; a node starting during the reset can outlive it until shutdown

glue.title: Glue Data Catalog
glue.summary: Create the databases, tables, and partitions that local Athena queries use.
features: Database CRUD, tags and pagination
Table CRUD and batch deletion
Partition CRUD, batch operations and partition listings
Names are normalized to lowercase; deleting a database removes its tables and partitions
gaps: Only Data Catalog operations are implemented
ETL jobs, crawlers, workflows and production engines are not implemented

athena.title: Athena
athena.summary: Query local S3 data through the Glue catalog using an in-memory SQLite SQL engine.
features: Workgroups, named queries, query execution metadata, pagination and client tokens
SELECT queries over CSV, delimited text and JSON, including gzip data
Glue catalog DDL, SHOW, DESCRIBE, MSCK REPAIR and partition changes
Query results are retained and written to the configured S3 output location
gaps: Queries complete inside StartQueryExecution; there is no distributed query engine
SQL is a documented SQLite-backed subset, not full Trino semantics
Parquet, ORC, Avro, Iceberg, CTAS and INSERT are rejected

sqs.title: SQS
sqs.summary: Use queues with visibility timeouts, long polling, FIFO ordering, and dead-letter workflows.
features: Queue lifecycle, attributes and tags
Send, receive, delete, visibility updates and batch operations
Long polling waits outside transactions
FIFO deduplication and group ordering
Dead-letter queues and message move tasks

AWS-style console with account/Region-scoped standard and FIFO queue creation and editing, message send/receive/details/delete/visibility controls, typed purge/delete confirmations, tags, access and redrive allow policies, and standard-queue DLQ redrive task management
PurgeQueue clears available, delayed and in-flight messages while preserving settings and enforcing a 60-second repeat-purge guard
gaps: No throughput enforcement or IAM/resource policy evaluation
No message groups on standard queues or FIFO message move tasks
DeleteQueue does not enforce the AWS name-reuse delay
Purge completes immediately instead of an asynchronous deletion window; FIFO deduplication history is retained
Console management requires parse mode; verify mode exposes queue inventory and requires signed CLI or SDK requests for actions

sns.title: SNS
sns.summary: Publish messages to local queues and functions, or confirmed HTTP subscriptions.
features: Topics, tags, subscriptions, filtering and FIFO deduplication
SQS fan-out and asynchronous Lambda invocation
HTTP/HTTPS confirmation and outbound delivery
Email and SMS deliveries are recorded for inspection

AWS-style console with account/Region-scoped standard and FIFO topic creation, display names, deduplication, policies and tags; subscription lists and details, endpoint selection, confirmation and deletion, raw delivery and attribute/body filters; message publishing and topic-specific delivery inspection
Topic attributes report confirmed and pending subscription counts separately; inventory exposes pending status and filter configuration without confirmation tokens
gaps: Email and SMS are recorded, not sent to providers
No mobile application or Firehose subscriptions, delivery retries or message signatures
Topic policies are stored but not evaluated; no cross-account subscriptions
Console management requires parse mode; verify mode exposes topic/subscription inventory and delivery history and requires signed CLI or SDK requests for actions

eventbridge.title: EventBridge
eventbridge.summary: Route events through local buses, patterns, rules, schedules, archives, and replays.
features: Default and custom buses, rules, targets and input transformers
Pattern matching shared with other event services
SQS, SNS and Lambda targets in the same account and region
Scheduled rules, durable retry records and SQS dead-letter queues
Archives and synchronous replay

AWS-style console for scoped event buses, rule patterns and schedules, nondelivering pattern tests, Lambda/SQS/SNS target selection and input/retry options, tags, explicit test-event publication and rule/bus delivery inspection
gaps: No partner buses, cross-account routing or additional target service families
Bus policies are stored but not evaluated
Replays run synchronously and cannot be cancelled
Cron does not support L, W or #
Verify mode exposes bus/rule/target inventory and deliveries; management and event publication require signed CLI/SDK requests
Bus permissions, archives and replay management use the AWS API rather than console forms

scheduler.title: EventBridge Scheduler
scheduler.summary: Run one-time, rate, and cron schedules against implemented services.
features: Schedule groups and schedule CRUD with time-zone handling
Background runner claims due schedules and invokes targets in-process
Failed deliveries can reach a target SQS dead-letter queue
gaps: No delivery retries; a failed run goes directly to its dead-letter queue
Flexible windows do not delay execution
ECS, SageMaker and CodeBuild templated targets are unsupported
KMS key ARNs are stored without customer-managed encryption

kinesis.title: Kinesis Data Streams
kinesis.summary: Write and read ordered shard records and feed local Lambda or Firehose consumers.
features: Streams, shards, consumers, shard iterators and record CRUD APIs
Split and merge shard metadata with stable record sequence ordering
Lambda mappings and Firehose sources read records in-process
gaps: No SubscribeToShard enhanced fan-out delivery or throughput enforcement
Resource policies, production record-size settings and warm throughput are outside the subset
KMS encryption settings are stored without encrypting stream records

firehose.title: Data Firehose
firehose.summary: Buffer direct or Kinesis records and deliver them to S3.
features: Delivery streams, tags, direct puts and batch puts
Background buffering and S3 output after size/time thresholds
Kinesis source polling and Lambda processing through the shared caller
gaps: Only S3 destinations are implemented
No HTTP, Redshift, OpenSearch, Splunk, Snowflake or Iceberg destinations
No MSK/database sources, dynamic partitioning, format conversion, encryption or S3 backup behavior

lambda.title: Lambda
lambda.summary: Manage functions and execute them in Docker using AWS runtime base images.
features: Function lifecycle, code from ZIP or S3, versions, aliases, layers and tags
LocalStack-compatible hot reload using S3Bucket=hot-reload and an absolute host directory; see [CLI and Terraform examples](../guides/lambda-hot-reload.md)
Synchronous and asynchronous invocation, retries and destinations
SQS, DynamoDB Streams and Kinesis event source mappings
Resource policies, function URLs and concurrency settings
Logs flow into CloudWatch Logs; tests use an in-process fake runtime

AWS-style console for scoped function creation/deletion, ZIP/S3/image deployment, execution roles, runtime/configuration/environment edits, tags, explicit sync/async/dry-run test invocation, SQS trigger settings, DynamoDB stream connections from table pages, SNS subscriptions and paginated CloudWatch logs
gaps: Executing deployed functions requires Docker
Hot reload mounts /var/task read-only and replaces warm containers on tree mtime/size/mode changes; compiled code must be rebuilt by the user
Hot reload does not support image packages, live layers, symlinks or special files; published versions retain a live directory reference rather than a code snapshot
Provisioned concurrency does not pre-start environments
Resource policies are stored but not evaluated
No ImageConfig or event sources beyond the three implemented families
Asynchronous work in flight is lost on restart
Console ZIP uploads and test events are limited to 1 MiB; larger deployment packages can be copied from S3
In identity.mode: verify the console shows function and trigger inventory; management, invocation and log reads require signed CLI/SDK requests
Console manages $LATEST; versions, aliases, layers, concurrency and function URLs use the AWS API
Reset ends event source mapping pollers and removes warm Docker containers; asynchronous invocations already running can still write records back

ec2.title: EC2
ec2.summary: Model networking and instance lifecycle for SDK and infrastructure tests.
features: VPCs, subnets, security groups, internet/NAT gateways and Elastic IPs
Route tables, network ACLs, VPC endpoints and derived network interfaces
Key pairs, instance records, instance profile associations and launch templates
Fixed regional image catalogue and tags
Resource inventory of taggable resources (not terminated instances or deleted NAT gateways), which the Resource Groups Tagging API finds and tags

AWS-style EC2 and VPC consoles with scoped instance launch/start/stop/reboot/termination, AMIs, generated/imported key pairs with one-time private key display, IAM instance profiles, VPC DNS settings and subnet public IPv4 settings, security rules, route tables and subnet associations, gateways, Elastic IPs, NAT gateways, network ACL rules and associations, endpoint configuration, tags, and links between related resources
gaps: Instances are records; no virtual machines boot and no guest software runs
Networking configuration does not create a real VPC, NAT or firewall
State transitions settle immediately
The large upstream EC2 API remains mostly outside the selected profile
Console AMIs and derived network interfaces are read-only; launch templates use the AWS CLI or SDK
Verify mode shows scoped inventory; detailed EC2/VPC reads and management require signed CLI/SDK requests

autoscaling.title: EC2 Auto Scaling
autoscaling.summary: Reconcile group membership with local EC2 instance records.
features: Groups, launch configurations, policies, scheduled actions and scaling activities
Desired count changes launch or terminate EC2 records outside transactions
Target tracking creates local CloudWatch alarms
gaps: No mixed-instance policies, warm pools, lifecycle hooks or instance refreshes
No load balancer attachments, predictive scaling, notification delivery or metrics collection
Instances remain metadata-only

ecr.title: ECR
ecr.summary: Manage repositories and push or pull images through a local Docker Registry API.
features: Repository lifecycle, tags, policies and lifecycle rules
Images, manifests, tags, layer uploads and download URLs
Authorization tokens scope Docker Registry requests
The gateway serves registry requests at /v2/
gaps: No replication, pull-through cache, scanning results, signing or KMS encryption
Registry policies and tag mutability exclusions are outside the subset
Deleted images do not trigger layer garbage collection

ecs.title: ECS
ecs.summary: Manage clusters, task definitions, tasks, and services with optional Docker execution.
features: Clusters, task definition revisions, service desired count and task lifecycle
Capacity provider metadata and tags
Optional Docker runner starts containers, exposes host ports and captures awslogs output
Services replace tasks when essential containers exit
gaps: Records mode starts no containers
Docker mode omits health checks, secrets, volumes, dependencies, task networking and resource limits
No container instances, load balancer integration, Service Connect, placement or execute command
Reset removes the task containers it started; a container starting during the reset can outlive it until shutdown

eks.title: EKS
eks.summary: Manage Kubernetes cluster metadata and optionally start local k3s API servers.
features: Clusters, node groups, Fargate profiles, add-ons and update metadata
Access entries, access policy associations, pod identity metadata and OIDC configuration
Optional privileged k3s container per cluster with an HTTPS proxy
EKS tokens map callers to the cluster account
gaps: Records mode starts no Kubernetes API
k3s mode makes accepted account principals administrators; IAM authorization is not reproduced
Cluster data and upgrades do not persist across restart
No Auto Mode, Outposts, hybrid nodes or CloudWatch log delivery
Reset removes the k3s containers it started; a cluster starting during the reset can outlive it until shutdown

apigateway.title: API Gateway REST APIs
apigateway.summary: Manage and invoke REST APIs with deployments, stages, proxy integrations, and authorizers.
features: Resource trees, methods, responses, integrations, deployments and stages
Lambda and HTTP proxy execution through gateway data routes
Lambda and Cognito authorizers, API keys and usage plan metadata
Custom domains, base path mappings and access logs

AWS-style console for scoped REST API creation and settings, resource trees and method/integration edits, authorizers, stage variables and access log settings, deployment snapshots, API/stage tags, and explicit deployed-stage request testing
gaps: No VTL integration mapping, non-proxy AWS/HTTP integrations, VPC links or request validation
Throttling, quotas, caching, canaries and authorizer caching are not enforced
No mutual TLS, import/export or general policy evaluation
Custom domains, response mappings, API keys and usage plans use the AWS API rather than console forms
Console management requires identity.mode: parse; verify mode retains resource inventory and requires signed CLI/SDK requests

Console test requests run deployed routing and authorizers without impersonating IAM; AWS_IAM routes require signed execute-api requests. The console action JSON envelope is limited to 2 MiB and displayed response bodies to 1 MiB; binary bodies display as base64

apigatewayv2.title: API Gateway HTTP APIs
apigatewayv2.summary: Manage and invoke HTTP APIs with routes, stages, proxy integrations, and JWT authorizers.
features: API, route, integration, deployment, stage and authorizer CRUD
Auto-deploy stages and Lambda proxy payload formats 1.0 and 2.0
HTTP forwarding, JWT and Lambda authorizers, access logs

AWS-style console for scoped HTTP API creation and CORS settings, routes, Lambda/HTTP integrations, JWT/Lambda authorizers, auto/manual stages, deployment snapshots, API/stage tags, and explicit deployed-stage request testing
gaps: WebSocket APIs are not implemented
No VPC links, parameter mappings, throttling, caching or authorizer caching
Only the selected HTTP API management members are supported
Custom domains and API mappings use the AWS API rather than console forms
Console management requires identity.mode: parse; verify mode retains resource inventory and requires signed CLI/SDK requests

Console test requests execute deployed snapshots; automatic stages publish draft changes immediately, manual stages require a new deployment. AWS_IAM tests require signed execute-api CLI/SDK requests. Console action JSON is limited to 2 MiB and displayed response bodies to 1 MiB; binary bodies display as base64

appsync.title: AppSync GraphQL
appsync.summary: Run GraphQL APIs with local resolvers and WebSocket subscriptions.
features: GraphQL APIs, API keys, schema/type operations, data sources, functions and resolvers
Unit and pipeline resolvers using APPSYNC_JS or a VTL subset
NONE, Lambda, HTTP, DynamoDB and EventBridge data sources
Authentication with API keys, IAM callers, Cognito, OIDC and Lambda
Lambda resolver batching and enhanced subscription filters
gaps: JavaScript utilities and VTL form a local subset of AppSync runtimes
Subscriptions live in memory and close on shutdown
AppSync Events is a separate unimplemented surface
Production scaling, caching and every upstream resolver/data-source option are not reproduced
Reset keeps real-time WebSocket connections and their subscriptions

elbv2.title: Elastic Load Balancing v2
elbv2.summary: Manage application and network load balancer metadata and invoke HTTP listener behavior.
features: Load balancers, target groups, targets, listeners, listener rules, attributes and tags
Fixed responses, redirects, Lambda targets and HTTP IP targets
Related subnet, security group and certificate checks through local services
gaps: No Gateway load balancers or real raw TCP/UDP forwarding
HTTPS listener metadata is served over plain HTTP; no TLS termination
No health probes, stickiness, authenticate actions, access-log delivery or capacity reservations
EC2 record targets cannot run applications

route53.title: Route 53
route53.summary: Manage hosted zones and record sets without running a DNS server.
features: Public and private hosted zones, record changes and pagination
Routing policy and alias metadata, VPC associations, health-check records and tags
Private zone VPCs are checked with local EC2
gaps: No DNS listener and no endpoint probing for health checks
No traffic policies, reusable delegation sets, query logging, DNSSEC or CIDR collections

cloudfront.title: CloudFront
cloudfront.summary: Manage distribution and origin access control metadata for infrastructure tests.
features: Distribution lifecycle and ETag-based updates
Alias uniqueness, caller-reference idempotency and tags
Origin access control lifecycle
gaps: No CDN caching, edge delivery or origin proxy runtime
Only selected distribution/configuration fields are implemented
CloudFront KeyValueStore is a separate future candidate

iam.title: IAM
iam.summary: Store account-wide identity resources and issue user access keys.
features: Roles, users, groups, membership and instance profiles
Inline and managed policies and policy attachments
OpenID Connect providers and access key lifecycle
Active IAM keys participate in gateway credential resolution

IAM console with account selection, guided user and role creation, group creation with users and policies, permission copying, inherited group permissions, multiple policy and membership changes, trust policies, EC2 instance profiles, tags, access keys and policy versions
gaps: Permission policies are stored but not evaluated
No AWS-managed policy catalogue, root access keys, login profiles or permissions boundaries
No access-key usage tracking
IAM console forms require parse mode; verify mode keeps the UI read-only and requires signed API requests
OIDC providers use the AWS API; console passwords, MFA, permissions boundaries and AWS-managed policy provisioning are not available in the console

sts.title: STS
sts.summary: Issue local session credentials and inspect the resolved caller identity.
features: GetCallerIdentity, AssumeRole, GetSessionToken and AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
Subset of role trust policies with AWS, Federated and Service principals
Session credentials feed signature verification and account resolution
In-process service role assumption supports the IoT credentials provider
gaps: Web identity token signatures are not checked by STS
No MFA, SAML, federation tokens, session tags or session policies
Temporary credentials used to create Lambda functions do not provide a usable runtime secret

cognitoidp.title: Cognito user pools
cognitoidp.summary: Manage users and clients, authenticate locally, and issue pool-signed JWTs.
features: User pools, app clients, users, groups, attributes and resource servers
Password and SRP flows, refresh tokens and pool RS256 JWTs
JWKS/OpenID configuration endpoints and client-credentials OAuth tokens
Selected Lambda triggers and inspectable verification/invitation messages
gaps: No hosted UI, pool domains, social identity providers or broader OAuth grants
No required MFA sign-in, custom/passwordless authentication, device tracking or threat protection
Messages are recorded in diagnostics rather than emailed/SMSed

cognitoidentity.title: Cognito identity pools
cognitoidentity.summary: Link supported logins to identities and exchange them for local STS role credentials.
features: Identity pools, identities, role mappings, developer tokens and login linking
Cognito user-pool and configured OIDC logins
Authenticated and unauthenticated role selection
Credential exchange through STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
gaps: Social login providers are rejected
STS and IAM limitations apply to issued credentials
Only selected pool and mapping members are implemented

kms.title: KMS
kms.summary: Exercise local cryptographic key and alias workflows.
features: Symmetric AES, HMAC and selected RSA/ECC key types
Encrypt/decrypt, re-encryption, data keys, signing and public-key retrieval
Key lifecycle, aliases, policies, grants and tags
SSM, Secrets Manager and SQS validate usable customer-managed keys
gaps: Policies and grants are stored but not evaluated
No key-material rotation, imports, custom key stores or multi-region keys
No KEY_AGREEMENT, secp256k1, SM2, ML-DSA or attestation recipient behavior
Local ciphertext formats are emulator-specific

acm.title: Certificate Manager
acm.summary: Issue or import local certificates and exercise certificate lifecycle APIs.
features: Certificate request, describe, listing, deletion and tags
Import/get/export, encrypted exported private keys and options
Requests issue immediately through a TinyStack certificate authority
Issuing helpers are shared with IoT
gaps: No DNS/email validation wait, Private CA, renewal or ACME
Only exportable certificates retain private keys
Certificates are local CA certificates, not publicly trusted

ssm.title: SSM Parameter Store
ssm.summary: Store versioned parameters, labels, tags, and hierarchy queries.
features: String, StringList and SecureString parameter records
Get by name/path, history, labels and version-aware updates
Public EC2 image parameters supplied from the local catalogue
Customer-managed KMS key usability checks
gaps: SecureString values are stored as plaintext; undecrypted reads return a placeholder
Only Parameter Store is implemented, not the broader Systems Manager API
No parameter policies, shared parameters, advanced data types or quotas

secretsmanager.title: Secrets Manager
secretsmanager.summary: Manage secret versions, staging labels, deletion windows, and Lambda rotation.
features: Secret lifecycle, binary/string values, version IDs and staging labels
Batch reads, tags and resource policy metadata
Four-step Lambda rotation with background scheduling
Customer-managed KMS key usability checks

AWS-style console for scoped secret creation, key/value or plaintext and binary values, explicit retrieve/hide/copy, password generation, versions and staging labels, metadata and KMS key edits, tags, resource policies, Lambda rotation configuration and immediate rotation, and scheduled deletion with restore or permanent deletion
gaps: No replication, managed/external rotation or enforced rotation windows
Resource policies are stored but not evaluated
Values remain local store data; KMS validation does not imply AWS at-rest encryption
Verify mode exposes secret metadata inventory; values, versions, policies, rotation and management require signed AWS CLI or SDK requests

logs.title: CloudWatch Logs
logs.summary: Inspect log events and route local subscription and metric filters.
features: Log groups, streams, retention metadata, tags and paged event reads
PutLogEvents and filter patterns
Subscription delivery to Lambda, Kinesis and Firehose
Metric filters publish local CloudWatch metrics
Logs Insights subset runs synchronously and retains query results

AWS-style console for scoped log groups and streams, retention and tags, explicit event searches with time/stream/term filters, older/newer event paging and details, individual event ingestion and Logs Insights results; Lambda monitor links open their log groups
gaps: Logs Insights is a local query-language subset
Production ingestion, retention scheduling and scale limits are not reproduced
Unselected log-management APIs are unsupported
Verify mode exposes group/stream inventory; event reads, queries and management require signed CLI/SDK requests
Subscription and metric filters use the AWS API rather than console forms

cloudwatch.title: CloudWatch metrics and alarms
cloudwatch.summary: Record metrics, evaluate alarms, and exercise local monitoring integrations.
features: Metrics, statistics, percentile queries and a metric-math subset
Metric/composite alarms, alarm history and dashboards
Background evaluation and state-change EventBridge events
SNS, Lambda and Auto Scaling actions through the caller

AWS-style console for scoped metric selection and graphs, explicit custom metric publication, metric/composite alarm creation and editing, actions and state tests, paginated history, tags, and dashboard JSON editing with metric/text previews
gaps: No anomaly detection, Metrics Insights, metric streams or insight rules
No EC2/Systems Manager actions or alarm mute rules
Services do not automatically publish AWS namespace metrics
Local retention is 15 days for datapoints and 30 days for alarm history
Verify mode exposes alarm and dashboard inventory; metric reads, configurations and management require signed CLI/SDK requests
Console graphs support up to ten selected metrics and 10,000 data points; partial results require a narrower range or larger period
Dashboard previews support metric queries and plain text, with up to ten queries and one Region per metric widget; other widget types and layout remain in source
Dashboards are scoped by account and Region locally; CloudWatch requests use the AWS signing name monitoring

cloudformation.title: CloudFormation
cloudformation.summary: Create and update local stacks through the same service operations used by SDK clients.
features: JSON/YAML templates, parameters, conditions, mappings, supported intrinsics and dependency ordering
Stack create/update/delete, rollback, change sets, events and exports
Typed resource registry with validated properties and attributes
Selected SAM resources and event transformations
Resource operations run outside store transactions through the lenient caller
gaps: Only resource types and properties registered in resources*.go are supported
No stack sets, nested stacks, custom resources, imports or drift detection
No macros/AWS::Include, policies with unsupported semantics or snapshot deletion behavior
IAM capabilities are checked but permission policies and service roles are not evaluated

sfn.title: Step Functions
sfn.summary: Execute a local Amazon States Language subset with service integrations.
features: State machines, versions, aliases, activities, executions and history
JSONPath and JSONata evaluation, supported state types, Retry/Catch and callbacks
In-process AWS SDK integrations can call implemented operations
TestState and redrive support
AWS-style console for scoped state machine creation, ASL validation and editing, execution roles, logging configuration and tags
Console starts and stops Standard executions with paginated execution history, input, output and failure details; Express workflows return synchronous results
gaps: No distributed Map, map runs, execution retention or IAM role checks
JSONPath filters and recursive descent are outside the subset
Running executions abort after restart; activity queues and task tokens are in memory
Express execution results are not retained; console results last until leaving or reloading the page
Versions, aliases, activities, TestState and redrive remain available through the AWS CLI or SDK; verify-mode console shows read-only inventory
Reset does not stop executions already running

sesv2.title: SES v2
sesv2.summary: Render and inspect email workflows without sending external mail.
features: Identities are verified immediately; templates and configuration sets are stored
SendEmail and bulk email validate senders and render a Handlebars subset
Delivery records contain messages; configuration set events reach SNS, EventBridge and Firehose
Mailbox simulator addresses generate bounce/complaint behavior
Identities, templates, configuration sets and send counts are shared with SES v1
gaps: No SMTP or real outbound email delivery
Identity verification is immediate; template rendering and sending limits are local approximations

ses.title: SES v1
ses.summary: Send and verify email with the classic SES Query API over the same state as SES v2.
features: Same signing name as SES v2: form requests reach v1 and REST JSON requests reach v2
VerifyEmailIdentity, VerifyEmailAddress, VerifyDomainIdentity and VerifyDomainDkim verify immediately, with three DKIM tokens for a domain
ListIdentities, GetIdentityVerificationAttributes, ListVerifiedEmailAddresses and DeleteIdentity read and write the identities SES v2 stores
SendEmail, SendRawEmail (MIME parsed with net/mail), SendTemplatedEmail and SendBulkTemplatedEmail check the sender, render templates, and record messages in the delivery log
CreateTemplate, GetTemplate, UpdateTemplate, DeleteTemplate and ListTemplates share SES v2 templates
CreateConfigurationSet, DeleteConfigurationSet, ListConfigurationSets and DescribeConfigurationSet share SES v2 configuration sets, whose events a send publishes
GetSendQuota and GetSendStatistics report the hourly send counts SES v2 keeps
gaps: No SMTP or real outbound email delivery

Configuration set event destinations, tracking, delivery and reputation options, receipt rules, identity policies, notification and MAIL FROM settings, and custom verification emails are not implemented
SendEmail rejects ReturnPath, SourceArn and ReturnPathArn; sending authorization is not evaluated
DescribeConfigurationSet returns only the name, and GetSendStatistics reports hourly rather than 15-minute data points with no bounces, complaints or rejects
Identity verification is immediate; domain verification tokens are derived from the domain

iot.title: IoT Core
iot.summary: Connect devices and manage registry, policies, rules, jobs, provisioning, and fleet searches.
features: Things, types, static group trees, certificates, registered CAs, policy versions and attachments
Per-account/region MQTT broker over WebSocket, optional TLS and plain TCP
Topic SQL, Basic Ingest, error actions and local service destinations
Custom Lambda authorizers and default authorizer selection
Deactivating or revoking a certificate, or deactivating its CA, disconnects its live MQTT clients with AUTH_ERROR
Snapshot jobs, MQTT job notifications and credentials-provider role aliases
Fleet provisioning templates with ownership tokens and optional hooks
Fleet indexing queries over registry, shadows and connectivity

Custom authorizer refreshAfterInSeconds is not acted on
No billing/dynamic groups, certificate transfers, CA auto-registration, continuous jobs or job rollout/retry/scheduling settings
Fleet SearchIndex scans local records; no aggregations, Device Defender or geolocation
MQTT session/in-flight state stays in memory; retained messages persist
Reset keeps connected MQTT clients and the broker's in-memory session state

Retained-message APIs and connection/subscription APIs
Shadow updates emit accepted/rejected/delta/documents MQTT messages
gaps: Publish userProperties requires generator support and is not implemented
MQTT broker accepts at most QoS 1 and 128 KB payloads
Connections and subscriptions are in memory
The SDK needs an explicit local BaseEndpoint override

iotjobsdataplane.title: IoT Jobs Data Plane

resourcegroups.title: Resource Groups
resourcegroups.summary: Group resources with tag-based or CloudFormation stack queries, resolved against the same resources the Tagging API lists.
features: CreateGroup, GetGroup, UpdateGroup, DeleteGroup and ListGroups with resource-type, configuration-type, owner, display-name and criticality filters and pagination
Groups addressed by name or ARN; names are unique per account and Region and are validated as the model specifies

TAG_FILTERS_1_0 queries with ResourceTypeFilters (AWS::AllSupported or CloudFormation-style types such as AWS::SQS::Queue) and TagFilters, evaluated against every service's resource inventory in the caller's account and Region
CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_1_0 queries that list a stack's resources, matched to inventory resources by physical ID
ListGroupResources with resource type filters and pagination, and SearchResources for ad hoc queries; unknown resource types and missing stacks are reported in QueryErrors
GetGroupQuery, UpdateGroupQuery, GetGroupConfiguration and PutGroupConfiguration
Tags on groups through Tag, Untag and GetTags, and through the Resource Groups Tagging API
GetAccountSettings and UpdateAccountSettings, which settle at once
Groups appear in the resource inventory
gaps: GroupResources and UngroupResources are not supported, so configuration-based groups have no members and ListGroupingStatuses is always empty
Group configurations are stored but not validated beyond their shape; service-linked behavior such as capacity reservation pools is not run
Resource types are derived from each inventory type (AWS::<Service>::<Type>); types of services TinyStack has no inventory for report RESOURCE_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED
Stack queries match resources by physical ID, so stack resources absent from the inventory are left out, and an inactive stack reports as not existing
Group lifecycle events and application tags are not emitted; the name/ID group form is not accepted
IAM policies are not evaluated

resourcegroupstaggingapi.title: Resource Groups Tagging API
resourcegroupstaggingapi.summary: Find and tag resources across services by tag, resource type, or ARN.
features: GetResources with tag filters, resource type filters, ARN lists and pagination
GetTagKeys and GetTagValues across the caller's account and Region
TagResources and UntagResources through each owning service's own tag operations, with per-resource failures
Reads every service's resource inventory; keeps no records of its own
Global IAM and Route 53 resources are reported to us-east-1 callers
gaps: Resources whose tags were all removed are not reported, unlike AWS's previously tagged resources
No compliance details, tag policies, report creation or TagsPerResource limits
CloudFormation stacks, ElastiCache and Auto Scaling resources cannot be tagged through this API

pipes.title: EventBridge Pipes
pipes.summary: Connect SQS queues and Kinesis or DynamoDB streams to targets with filtering and Lambda enrichment.
features: CreatePipe, DescribePipe, UpdatePipe, DeletePipe, ListPipes with filters and pagination, StartPipe and StopPipe
Pipes settle at once in RUNNING or STOPPED; responses report the transitional state
Tags on pipes through TagResource, UntagResource and ListTagsForResource, and through the Resource Groups Tagging API
SQS sources read in-process; messages are deleted after delivery or when a filter drops them
Kinesis and DynamoDB stream sources with TRIM_HORIZON or LATEST and a per-pipe cursor
FilterCriteria event patterns shared with Lambda event source mappings
Lambda enrichment, and InputTemplate with JSON paths and aws.pipes variables on enrichment and target
Lambda, SQS, SNS, EventBridge, Step Functions and Kinesis targets, called in-process; Lambda and Step Functions receive the batch as a JSON array
Resources appear in the resource inventory
gaps: MQ, Kafka, MSK and other sources, and ECS, Batch, Firehose, HTTP and other targets fail CreatePipe explicitly
No batching windows, parallelization, dead-letter queues, retry limits or partial batch failure handling; a failed delivery is retried on the next visit
AT_TIMESTAMP starting positions, log configuration and KMS keys are not supported

JSON paths in EventBridge target parameters and [*] wildcards in templates are not supported
Role ARNs are checked for shape only; IAM policies are not evaluated

cloudcontrol.title: Cloud Control API
cloudcontrol.summary: Manage live S3 buckets and SQS queues with the CloudFormation resource handlers and a durable request journal.
features: CreateResource, GetResource, UpdateResource, DeleteResource and ListResources for AWS::S3::Bucket and AWS::SQS::Queue
BucketName, Tags and VersioningConfiguration.Status (Enabled or Suspended) for buckets; queue names, FIFO settings, supported queue attributes and tags for queues
Generated resource names when omitted; identifiers are bucket names or queue URLs, as in the resource schemas
Reads live state from S3 and SQS, including resources created directly or through CloudFormation; lists identifiers with pagination
RFC 6902 JSON Patch updates with add, remove, replace, move, copy and test; create-only and read-only changes fail explicitly
Synchronous writes return SUCCESS or FAILED ProgressEvents with modeled handler error codes and request tokens
GetResourceRequestStatus and paginated ListResourceRequests with operation and status filters; request history is account/Region scoped and visible for seven days
ClientToken replays the original progress event for 36 hours and rejects conflicting requests; concurrent writes to the same resource are rejected
Request history and client tokens survive persistent restart; interrupted writes become FAILED and release resource locks
Created resources appear under S3 or SQS in the console inventory, Resource Groups and Tagging API; Cloud Control creates no separate resource copies
gaps: Only AWS::S3::Bucket and AWS::SQS::Queue are exposed, even though CloudFormation supports more resource types
No asynchronous polling, cancellation, hooks, private type versions or role assumption; CancelResourceRequest is not selected, and RoleArn, TypeVersionId and ListResources.ResourceModel are rejected
Bucket configuration beyond tags and versioning, queue Policy and any properties outside the shared handler subset are rejected
Writes may partially apply before a downstream failure or process interruption; no automatic rollback or replay of interrupted writes
ListResources returns identifiers; GetResource returns the supported live properties and read-only Arn (and QueueUrl for queues)
Resource models contain only the supported property subset; general IAM permission evaluation is not implemented

rds.title: RDS
rds.summary: Manage PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB instances with an optional Docker database runtime.
features: Create, describe, modify, stop, start, reboot and delete scoped DB instances; modeled duplicate, missing and state errors
PostgreSQL majors 14, 15, 16 (default), 17 map to postgres:<major>; MySQL 8.0 maps to mysql:8.0; MariaDB 11 maps to mariadb:11; other engines and versions fail explicitly
Describe instances supports db-instance-id, engine and db-subnet-group exact-value filters; MaxRecords 20–100 and Marker pagination also work for subnet and parameter group lists
Subnet groups validate existing EC2 subnets in one VPC; parameter groups are records with engine-family validation and in-use deletion checks
Instance and group tags, diagnostic inventory and Resource Groups Tagging API integration
CloudFormation AWS::RDS::DBInstance and AWS::RDS::DBSubnetGroup with selected properties
Set rds.instances: docker to start real databases; default rds.instances: records returns available records immediately
Docker uses credentials and database names in engine image environment variables, free host ports bound to 127.0.0.1, and TCP plus pg_isready/mysqladmin ping/mariadb-admin ping readiness checks
Named volumes per account/Region/instance retain SQL data across container and persistent TinyStack restarts; available instances recreate or reattach containers from stored records

StopDBInstance stops the container, StartDBInstance starts it, and RebootDBInstance restarts it; TinyStack shutdown removes containers and retains volumes; reset and deletion remove containers and volumes
MasterUserPassword changes execute ALTER ROLE/ALTER USER in Docker; DBInstanceClass and AllocatedStorage are metadata; modifications apply immediately
Startup removes orphaned RDS containers and volumes whose ownership ARN has no instance record
Omitted DBName uses the instance identifier with hyphens replaced by underscores for the Docker database name; default AllocatedStorage is 20 GiB of metadata
CloudFormation DBInstance creation waits for availability before publishing endpoint attributes

AWS-style scoped console for databases, engine selection, connection commands and URLs, status polling, immediate password/class changes, tags, stop/start/reboot, confirmed deletion without snapshots, and subnet and parameter group creation and deletion
gaps: Records mode has no SQL listener: endpoints use 127.0.0.1 and the engine default port, matching the ElastiCache records-only convention
AllocatedStorage does not enforce a volume size; DBInstanceClass does not change CPU or memory limits; network topology and AWS availability behavior are not reproduced
EngineVersion accepts only the listed major tags, not arbitrary AWS minor/patch versions; image tags are floating within the chosen major
Parameter groups are records only; engine parameters are not applied

Snapshots, replicas, clusters/Aurora, Multi-AZ, IAM DB authentication, managed master passwords/Secrets Manager, option groups, events and proxies are unsupported; input members outside the profile fail explicitly
Delete requires SkipFinalSnapshot=true; final snapshots and snapshot identifiers are rejected; ApplyImmediately=false rejects deferred changes
Host ports can change after container recreation; no advertise host setting exists, so a remote Docker daemon is unsupported

Persistent records retain database credentials in the local store; memory-mode shutdown retains volumes without records, so delete or reset before shutdown to remove SQL data immediately; startup removes orphaned runtime resources
Failed initial startup or readiness timeout marks the instance failed and removes its container and fresh volume; recovery failures retain an existing volume
CloudFormation endpoint attributes do not refresh when a later container recreation changes the host port
Verify mode exposes database metadata inventory; RDS management and full group metadata require signed AWS CLI or SDK requests

organizations.title: Organizations
organizations.summary: Manage global organization, account, hierarchy and SCP records.
features: Create/describe/delete an organization with ALL (default) or CONSOLIDATED_BILLING; caller becomes the management account

Root and OU hierarchy with five nested OU levels, duplicate-name checks, empty-OU and member-free organization deletion
SCP JSON records, policy attachments and root enable/disable; AWS-managed FullAWSAccess is attached by default

Tags, inventory, Resource Groups Tagging API and console catalogue; CloudFormation OrganizationalUnit and Policy selected properties

Management account email/name are local defaults (<account>@tinystack.local and Management account); account removal does not implement AWS billing prerequisites

Input members outside the generated profile and unsupported enum/filter values fail explicitly

servicediscovery.title: Cloud Map
servicediscovery.summary: Manage regional Cloud Map records and discover registered instances through the SDK data plane.

Service records with DNS routing/TTL configuration and custom health checks; empty-service/namespace deletion checks and duplicate-name errors
Register/deregister/get/list instances, health status and immediate custom-health changes; service instance revisions update with registrations and health changes

DiscoverInstances supports required QueryParameters, preferred OptionalParameters with fallback, HEALTHY (default), UNHEALTHY, ALL and HEALTHY_OR_ELSE_ALL filtering, MaxResults 1–1000 and DiscoverInstancesRevision
Namespace filters TYPE/NAME/HTTP_NAME, service filter NAMESPACE_ID and operation STATUS/TYPE/NAMESPACE_ID/SERVICE_ID filters; EQ/IN (one value) and BEGINS_WITH; list pagination MaxResults 1–100
Regional/account-scoped records, resource tags, diagnostic inventory, Resource Groups Tagging API and official-icon console catalogue
CloudFormation HttpNamespace, PrivateDnsNamespace, Service and Instance with selected properties; operations complete synchronously

Instance attributes are records; no ECS task registration, DNS validation/probing or asynchronous health propagation
CloudFormation public namespace and advanced properties, and management console pages are unsupported
Unknown filter names/conditions and profile-excluded input members fail explicitly

SDKs prefix DiscoverInstances hosts with data-, so http://localhost:4566 or an IP endpoint becomes an unresolvable data-localhost; use http://tinystack.localhost:4566 (data-tinystack.localhost resolves to loopback per RFC 6761) or disable the host prefix in the client (Go: smithyhttp.DisableEndpointHostPrefix)

account.title: AWS Account
account.slice: Implement `GetAccountInformation`, `GetContactInformation`, and `ListRegions` for the caller's account.
account.features:
- [ ] `GetAccountInformation` — return `AccountId`, `AccountName`, `AccountCreatedDate`, and `AccountState` through `POST /getAccountInformation`.
- [ ] `GetContactInformation` — return configured primary contact details through `POST /getContactInformation`.
- [ ] `ListRegions` — return region opt-in statuses through `POST /listRegions`, with `RegionOptStatusContains`, `MaxResults`, and `NextToken`.
- [ ] `GetRegionOptStatus` — validate `RegionName` and return the same status as `ListRegions` through `POST /getRegionOptStatus`.
- [ ] Additive `AccountState` — populate `ACTIVE` by default. The field was added on 2026-04-29; newer SDKs expose it while older JSON SDK models can ignore it.
account.integration: Use the AWS Account `2021-02-01` REST JSON model and SigV4 signing name `account`. Resolve the account through `identity.accounts` or `defaults.account`; keep account details and region statuses consistent across calls and restarts. Serve only the caller's account until Organizations delegation exists, and reject another explicit `AccountId`. Encode modeled status codes and errors through the REST JSON codec.
account.acceptance: Call all four paths through an AWS SDK and raw REST JSON requests. Check account isolation, validation errors, region filtering and pagination, and consistent opt-in statuses. Confirm `AccountState` in raw responses and current SDKs, compatibility with an older SDK model, and stable configured details after restart.

opensearch.title: OpenSearch Service
opensearch.slice: create one OpenSearch domain, obtain its endpoint, index a document, search it, and delete the domain through AWS-style management calls.
opensearch.features:
- [ ] Management — Create/describe/list/delete domains, plus supported configuration updates and tags. Return creation and processing states tied to real engine health.
- [ ] Runtime — Start a pinned OpenSearch image with bounded memory, isolated data volume, and reachable endpoint. Route domain data-plane requests to that engine.
- [ ] Persistence — Reconnect to the same volume on persistent restart; define cleanup on domain deletion and failed creation.
- [ ] Later features — Multi-node clusters, VPC networking, fine-grained access control, custom endpoints, encryption settings, snapshots, and serverless collections require separate designs.
opensearch.integration:
Domain metadata is regional and account-scoped. The provider handles AWS
management requests; the engine handles indexing and search. Do not claim AWS
security or cluster topology features from an unconfigured single container.
Proxy/routing must select a domain without leaking one account’s index to
another. Runtime launch and health checks happen outside storage transactions.
opensearch.acceptance:
Create a domain with an AWS SDK, wait until available, index and search through
the returned endpoint, restart, and delete. Verify index isolation, unsupported
configuration errors, failed launch cleanup, memory/port limits, tags, and
management response parity against AWS captures.
